ام شب، شب ماتم حسینا

۱
لاچار لاچار حسینا

۲
مظلوم حسینا، بے یار حسینا

۳
جو کر نہ سکی بھائی کا دیدار وہ بہنا
مظلوم حسینا مظلوم حسینا
بابا تھا جس کا حیدر کرار وہ بہنا
مظلوم حسینا مظلوم حسینا

۴
کوئی نہ رہا جس کا مددگار وہ بہنا
مظلوم حسینا مظلوم حسینا

مظلوم حسینا مظلوم حسینا

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/im-shab-shab-e-matam-e-husaina.md')
original = p.read_bytes()
head, tail = original.split(b'romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)
_, body = tail.split(b'\\n---\\n', 1)
roman = \"\"\"Im shab, shab-e-maatam-e-Husaina

1
Laachaar laachaar Husaina

2
Mazlum Husaina, be yaar Husaina

3
Jo kar na saki bhaai ka didaar woh behna
Mazlum Husaina mazlum Husaina
Baaba tha jis ka Haider-e-Karraar woh behna
Mazlum Husaina mazlum Husaina

4
Koi na raha jis ka madadgaar woh behna
Mazlum Husaina mazlum Husaina
Tathir ki waaris jo thi laachaar woh behna
Mazlum Husaina mazlum Husaina

5
R qaum meiṅ hota hai mazlum ka maatam
Zahra ke dil o jaan ka, maasum ka maatam
Qurbaani-e-Shabbir ko bhula na zamaana
Har ek ko ro ro ke rulaata hai Muharram
Aashur ka din yaad dilaata hai Muharram
Waajib hai ye paighaam zamaane ko sunaana
Ham zikr-e-shahidaan-e-wafa karte raheṅ ge
Abbas ke parcham ko sada uncha rakheṅ ge
Ye pursa hai Zahra ko safiraan-e-aza ka\"\"\"
block = '\\n'.join('  ' + line if line else '' for line in roman.splitlines())
updated = head + b'romanLyrics: |-\\n' + block.encode() + b'\\n---\\n' + body
assert updated.split(b'\\n---\\n', 1)[1] == original.split(b'\\n---\\n', 1)[1]
def counts(lyrics, digits):
    return [sum(line not in digits for line in stanza.splitlines()) for stanza in lyrics.strip().split('\\n\\n')]
assert counts(roman, '12345') == counts(body.decode(), '۱۲۳۴۵') == [1, 1, 1, 4, 4, 9]
p.write_bytes(updated)
PY

item.text:
Audited and updated the Roman transliteration. It now follows the Urdu preamble and five stanzas, with 20 aligned verse lines. I normalized spellings, restored missing lines and refrains from the Urdu, and removed extra repetitions. The Urdu body and metadata were preserved.

Two readings need editorial sign-off. The first line of stanza 5 begins with `ر قوم`, rendered `R qaum`, and `رکھں گے` is rendered `rakheṅ ge` based on the existing Roman.
